atoms.span: The Pile is an 825 GiB to 886 GB open-source English text dataset created by EleutherAI
created by EleutherAI and released on December 31, 2020
open-source English text dataset created by EleutherAI and released on December 31, 2020, to train large language models (LLMs).
Combines 22 diverse sub-datasets across academic, web, prose, and code domains.
Designed to improve cross-domain knowledge, reasoning, and generalization compared to raw web scrapes like Common Crawl.

mt: 'THE PILE DATASET' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE DATASET ITEMIZED, ALL TWENTY-TWO COMPONENTS; BOOKS3 AS 'LONG-FORM LITERARY TEXT', ITS PIRATED SOURCE, ITS REMOVAL AND THE AUTHORS' SUIT GIVEN AS 'CONTENT ADJUSTMENTS'
d: THE DATASET, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The Pile is an 825 GiB to 886 GB open-source English text dataset created by EleutherAI and released on December 31, 2020, to train large language models (LLMs).' Key overview (size, '~825 GiB compressed (zstandard format) containing roughly 300 billion tokens'; composition; purpose; 'Notable Models Trained On It: GPT-Neo, GPT-J, and the Pythia suite by EleutherAI'); the 22 sub-datasets, numbered, 'Books3 (Long-form literary text/books)' third and 'Gutenberg (PG-19) (Public domain literature)' eleventh; controversies and evolution ('resulting in content adjustments'; Common Pile v0.1). Eight cards: the Pile's home page, Wikipedia, Hugging Face, Reddit r/MachineLearning, the Pile's paper page, a YouTube paper reading, Hugging Face on the Common Pile v0.1, Michael Brenndoerfer.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the dataset, the Overview gives its maker, date, size, purpose and the models trained on it, lists its twenty-two components with a gloss on each, and closes on its copyright disputes and its licensed successor.
findings: THE LAYER ITEMIZED. The twenty-two components in the order of Wikipedia's size table, Pile-CC first and Enron Emails last, each with a gloss; the size given both ways, '825 GiB to 886 GB', the home page's 'The Pile is a 825 GiB diverse, open source language modelling data set' beside Wikipedia's 'The Pile is an 886 GB diverse, open-source dataset'. The census row reads a work's entry into the layer as membership of a component; the composition names the components and no work and no author in any of them. 'roughly 300 billion tokens' and the three model families are on no saved source; the Hugging Face card gives '100B<1T tokens'.

BOOKS3 GLOSSED. 'Books3 (Long-form literary text/books)'. Wikipedia: 'The Books3 component of the dataset contains copyrighted material compiled from Bibliotik, a piracy website.' and 'Books3 was removed from the Pile before a class action lawsuit was filed in 2024 by three authors'. The composition: 'The dataset encountered copyright challenges regarding specific components like Books3 and subtitles, resulting in content adjustments.' The source, the Rights Alliance's DMCA takedown of July 2023, the removal and the three authors' suit are absent; the census row reads that suit as 'the field's clearest case of works found in the layer under their authors' names after the fact'.

THE SUBTITLES AND THE SITE. 'subtitles' stands beside Books3 without its account ('Tens of thousands of YouTube videos had their subtitles scraped directly from YouTube and included in the Pile, which YouTube argued is against its terms of service'). Wikipedia's 'By 2024, The Pile also was taken down from its original site' is absent, and the first card is the original site's home page ('An 800GB Dataset of Diverse Text for Language Modeling What is the Pile?'), which the census also fetched with HTTP 200 on 2026-11-01 and which still reads 'Download Pile' and 'The Pile is hosted by the Eye .'

WHAT THE APPARATUS MAKES. 'Designed to improve cross-domain knowledge, reasoning, and generalization compared to raw web scrapes like Common Crawl.' The paper: 'models trained on the Pile improve significantly over both Raw CC and CC-100 on all components of the Pile'. The census row's 'makes' is the trained model scored on the Pile's own benchmark ('Pile BPB is a measure of world knowledge and reasoning ability in these domains'); the composition names models trained on it and does not carry the benchmark. The paper's 'we document potentially concerning aspects of the data for prospective users' is absent.

THE SUCCESSOR. 'EleutherAI introduced ethical alternatives such as Common Pile v0.1 using licensed text.' Wikipedia: 'released Common Pile v0.1, a training dataset that contains only works where the licenses permit their use for training AI models', 'In June 2025, EleutherAI, in partnership with the Poolside , Hugging Face , and the US Library of Congress'. The composition gives EleutherAI alone and no date; the seventh card carries the date in EleutherAI's words ('Four and a half years ago, EleutherAI entered the AI scene by releasing the Pile').
analysis: The dataset composed at its grain and itemized to its twenty-two components, the training layer named as the census row names it. Its literary component is glossed by genre, and the pirated source, the removal and the authors' suit that put works in it under their authors' names are reduced to 'content adjustments'.
per_note: EleutherAI named in the body; Leo Gao and Stella Biderman on the Hugging Face card; the home page, paper page and Wikipedia carded.
